title: Roasted Stuffed Pork Loin
conventions: buy strings are cook measures (what goes in the pot). Grams are TARGET-scale: the mapper states them where its printed measure quantizes away from the exact scale, and otherwise they are parse-compute's source-basis weight for that line multiplied by scale_factor exactly once.

new_commodity_proposals.evidence: Rapini is a distinct brassica sold as a leafy bunch, not a crown of broccoli, and it is routinely two to three times broccoli's price per pound; the board's broccoli match is a different food. A prior ruling this run already settled the identical phrase to broccoli-rabe, so if that id exists this is a REUSE and no new mint is needed, exactly like the brown-lentils case where only the vocabulary row was missing.

Dry-cured, unsmoked Italian ham sold in 3 to 4 oz packs at roughly 10 to 16 dollars a pound. It is not deli-ham (cooked, wet-cured lunch meat at about 5 dollars a pound), not spiral-ham or diced-ham (cooked whole-muscle roast and convenience dice), and not bacon or pancetta (smoked or belly cuts). The estate's own lookup for this term found no commodity in any namespace and no capture match, and no vocabulary row shares a core word with it. A prior ruling in this same run already settled the identical phrase to this id, so if it has since been minted this is a REUSE and not a proposal.

A separate shelf product from balsamic vinegar: the vinegar is reduced with sweetener to a pourable syrup, printing 40 cal and 10 g carbs per tbsp against vinegar's 15 cal and 3 g, in a squeeze bottle at a higher price per ounce. Bridging it to balsamic-vinegar would be wrong on price and on gram weight, which is why the pre-resolve flagged the syrup/vinegar form difference rather than aliasing it. Board reports no commodity and no capture match. A prior ruling this run used this same id for the identical phrase.

registrar_rulings.reason: No 'rabe' or 'rapini' string exists in commodities.json, recipe-commodities.json, recipe-board-everyday.json, or smp-feed.json (re-grepped, not just the dossier's word-overlap sweep), and recipe-floor-id-map.json names no pair. The near rows are different purchases: broccoli ($2.09/lb Aldi) is the crown vegetable, broccolini ($3.99/each) is the broccoli-gai-lan hybrid stalk, and rapini is a bitter turnip-family leafy bunch typically 2-3x broccoli's per-lb price - aliasing to either would silently misprice the recipe. SAME FOOD DIFFERENT... no: different food entirely, so new id in the weekly-staples namespace (commodities.json + capture worklist, unit lb) with allowlist pairs broccoli-rabe/broccoli and broccoli-rabe/broccolini recorded in commodity-dupe-allowlist.json ('distinct brassica species, 2-3x price spread'). Include should require rabe|rapini contiguously ('broccoli\s+rabe', '\brapini\b'); exclude must cover broccolini, baby broccoli, florets, frozen, and seasoning/pesto look-alikes at neighboring-commodity rigor before capture. Separately for the vocabulary: no ingredients.json row exists, so a new name row 'Broccoli Rabe' is also needed - a distinct edit through the sanctioned editor, not a side effect of this id ruling. Note to caller: id exists nowhere and is NOT priced; the recipe stays unpriced until capture runs.

No 'prosciutto', 'parma', 'speck', 'capicola', or 'dry-cured' string exists anywhere in the three namespaces or the live feed (re-grepped directly; the dossier's near rows were all coincidental 'sliced' word matches). The only plausible carrier is deli-ham ($0.1238/oz, include '\bham\b') - a cooked wet-cured lunch meat at roughly a third of prosciutto's ~$10-16/lb; same animal, different cure, different form, different purchase, so reuse would price the wrong food. New id in the recipe-only namespace (recipe-board-everyday baseline + recipe-commodities.json for sales) unless it earns weekly-staple status, unit oz, with allowlist pair prosciutto/deli-ham ('dry-cured vs cooked deli ham, ~3x price'). Include on 'prosciutto' contiguously; excludes must block prosciutto-WRAPPED prepared items (wrapped asparagus/mozzarella, pizzas, charcuterie sampler trays, 'prosciutto style' turkey) at ~150-pattern rigor. Also flag the seam this mint creates: deli-ham's bare '\bham\b' include will claim any product named 'Prosciutto Ham', so deli-ham needs a 'prosciutto' exclude added in the same edit or the audit pages Brad on day one. Vocabulary: no ingredients.json row shares a core word; a new 'Prosciutto' name row is a separate required edit. Not priced today - capture needed.

The estate itself already ruled this a different product: balsamic-vinegar's exclude list carries '\bglaze\b' and 'reduction' in BOTH commodities.json (line 43676) and recipe-commodities.json (line 466, with the note 'excludes glaze/reduction (sweetened, pricier per-oz)') - the vinegar id deliberately refuses this food, so aliasing to balsamic-vinegar ($0.1704/floz) would price a 15-cal vinegar for a 40-cal sweetened syrup and contradict the estate's own rules. No 'balsamic-glaze' id or feed cell exists; the only feed 'glaze' hit is Kikkoman sweet soy glaze under an unrelated id. SAME FOOD, DIFFERENT FORM -> different purchase: new id in the recipe-only namespace, unit floz, allowlist pair balsamic-glaze/balsamic-vinegar ('reduced+sweetened syrup vs straight vinegar; vinegar id already excludes glaze/reduction'). Include 'balsamic\s+(?:glaze|reduction)'; exclude vinaigrette/dressing/marinade/spray and glazed-snack look-alikes at neighboring rigor - this passes the dupe audit only WITH the allowlist entry, so ship them together. Vocabulary: nearest row is Balsamic Vinegar, different form, so a new 'Balsamic Glaze' name row is also needed as its own edit. Not priced today - capture needed.

macro_cross_check: Source published 540 cal / 47 carbs / 43 g protein per serving at 8 servings. Computed from the food DB at source scale over all 22 lines: about 4133 cal, 326 g protein and 391 g carbs total, which is 517 cal / 40.8 g protein / 48.9 g carbs per serving. Protein is 5.1 percent under the published figure and carbs are 4 percent over, both well inside tolerance, so the pork loin at 1360.8 g and the 113.4 g of prosciutto are the right portions. CALLED OUT: protein clears this run's 40 g floor by only 0.8 g per serving, so any downward revision of the pork loin weight or of the prosciutto (for example treating 4 oz as post-trim) drops this recipe below the floor. Calories sit comfortably in the 450 to 800 band. The brine sugar and salt are counted as purchased and the sugar's 250 cal are counted in full even though most of the brine is discarded, which is the conservative direction.
